about: The Te Deum is an ancient hymn of praise and thanksgiving. In it the Church confesses the majesty of the Holy Trinity, addresses Christ as King of glory and Judge, and then asks for salvation, protection and mercy. This edition retains the full traditional Roman text through its final act of trust.

seg.tr: We praise Thee, O God; we acknowledge Thee to be the Lord.

ex.w006: In the hymn the verb means publicly to confess and acknowledge God as Lord.

seg.tr: Thee, the Father everlasting, all the earth doth worship.
To Thee all Angels; to Thee the heavens and all the Powers:
to Thee the Cherubim and Seraphim continually cry:

ex.w027: The Cherubim and Seraphim continually take up the threefold “Holy”.

seg.tr: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of Sabaoth.
Heaven and earth are full of the majesty of Thy glory.
Thee, the glorious choir of the Apostles; Thee, the admirable company of the Prophets,
Thee, the white-robed army of the Martyrs, doth praise.

ex.w052: The adjective presents the martyrs as an army clothed in the white robes of victory.

seg.tr: Thee throughout the world
the holy Church doth acknowledge:
the Father of infinite majesty; Thy adorable, true and only Son;
also the Holy Ghost, the Comforter. Thou, O Christ, art the King of glory.

ex.w078: From this point the hymn addresses Christ directly.

seg.tr: Thou art the everlasting Son of the Father. When Thou didst take upon Thee to deliver man,

ex.w087: The participle with purpose phrase “ad liberándum” speaks of freely undertaking man's deliverance.

seg.tr: Thou didst not disdain the Virgin's womb.

ex.w092: The negation speaks not of disgust but of Christ's humble acceptance of true Incarnation from the Virgin.

seg.tr: Having overcome the sting of death,
Thou didst open the kingdom of heaven to all believers.
Thou sittest at the right hand of God, in the glory of the Father.
We believe that Thou shalt come to be our Judge.

ex.w112: The passive “créderis” means: we believe that Thou wilt come as Judge.

seg.tr: We therefore pray Thee to help Thy servants,
whom Thou hast redeemed with Thy Precious Blood.
Make them to be numbered with Thy Saints in glory everlasting.

ex.w130: The selected recension asks that God's servants be numbered among the Saints in everlasting glory.

seg.tr: Save Thy people, O Lord, and bless Thy inheritance.
Govern them, and raise them up for ever.
Every day we bless Thee.
and we praise Thy name for ever, yea, for ever and ever.
Vouchsafe, O Lord, this day to keep us without sin.
Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us. Let Thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, as we have hoped in Thee.
In Thee, O Lord, have I hoped; I shall not be confounded for ever.

ex.w194: The closing act of trust asks that hope placed in the Lord may never end in shame.
